subject: MedicaCare: processing locus & cross-border transfer Q&A
messages:
From: Daniel Smith <daniel.smith@medica-care.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medica-care.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions about where MedicaCare customer data is processed

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — MedicaCare is very interested in Redwood's latency profile and routing controls for clinical summarization workloads. Before we progress to procurement we have a brief set of questions for our security and privacy team about where requests are executed and whether any data crosses borders. Can you confirm the following at a high level?

1) Where is inference executed for requests originating from our US region (east coast)? Which cloud regions / countries could execute the work?
2) Which subprocessors (compute, networking, monitoring) may see transient data? We need a list of subprocessors + processing locations if possible.
3) Do you ever egress or persist customer payloads outside of the requested region? Any caching or longer-term storage?
4) Retention and deletion model — how quickly can customer data and logs be erased after a retention/contract request? What controls exist for on-prem or VPC customers?

We need this for our vendor risk assessment. If you can point us to a short evidence bundle (one-pager + subprocessor list) that's ideal.

Best,
Daniel
Daniel Smith
Senior Security Analyst — MedicaCare Inc.
security@medica-care.com

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Smith <daniel.smith@medica-care.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about where MedicaCare customer data is processed

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and I attached a concise processing matrix that maps common request flows to execution locations. Also cc'ing Marissa (privacy) and Connor (platform) to add any technical detail I miss.

Short answers (high level):
- Execution loci for US-origin requests: By default requests hitting our hosted API are routed to the nearest Redwood-hosted region (us-east1 or us-west2, depending on latency and capacity). In practice, most MedicaCare traffic from the east coast will land in us-east1 (Virginia) unless you request region pinning.
- Cross-border transfers: We do not intentionally egress production request payloads to EU/APAC regions for US customer traffic. Fallback routing can be configured but is off by default; any cross-region fallback uses compatible model variants and is logged.
- Subprocessors: Transient processing occurs on our compute pool (Redwood-managed GCP/Azure instances) and at a small set of telemetry vendors for monitoring/alerts. See attached Subprocessor_Register_2026.csv for full roster.
- Persistence & caching: We employ ephemeral KV cache for inference acceleration; by default KV entries are transient (ttl minutes) and are not persisted in long-term storage. Request logs (metadata, timestamps, latency) are retained for diagnostics. Full payload retention is off by default for hosted customers; private/Dedicated options offer stronger guarantees (no shared compute, customer-managed VPC).
- Deletion: For hosted customers we support API-driven deletion and account erasure with deletion timelines documented in the matrix. Typical erase of ephemeral logs and caches is within 48 hours; persistent backups and audit logs follow a 30–90 day window depending on the evidence bucket and your contract. For Private (VPC/on-prem) customers, you can request write-once erasure flows and KMS key rotation to render data inaccessible immediately.

Attachments included: Data_Processing_Matrix.pdf (brief mapping), Subprocessor_Register_2026.csv (ROSTER).

If helpful I can produce a one-page summary extract that maps to the exact MedicaCare control ids — would you like that?

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Smith <daniel.smith@medica-care.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about where MedicaCare customer data is processed

Hi Daniel — adding a few specifics for your security team to consume directly:

- Subprocessor list (high-level):
  * Compute: GCP (us-east1), Azure (eastus2) — both operated under Redwood-managed projects when on hosted.
  * Storage/Backups: GCS/Azure Blob — used only for customer-requested persistent storage or optional audit exports; not used for default inference payloads.
  * Monitoring: Datadog (US regions), Sentry (US) — only metadata/metrics, no full request payloads.
  * Key management: Redwood integrates with cloud KMS and offers customer-managed keys (Bring Your Own Key) for Private customers.
  * Network/CDN: Fastly/Cloudflare for edge routing; payloads are TLS-encrypted in transit and edges strictly forward to Redwood regions.

- Cross-border policy: For hosted customers we adhere to region pinning on request. If a customer explicitly opts in to multi-region routing (for HA), we document the allowed regions and obtain sign-off. We never unilaterally move customer payloads between continents.

- Deletion evidence: For MedicaCare we can provide a deletion log extract showing the timestamped erasure of the request artifacts and a key-rotation certificate if you elect BYOK. Formal erasure timelines:
  * Ephemeral caches & live KV: typically cleared within 0–2 hours of TTL or explicit delete.
  * Request logs (diagnostic metadata): up to 30 days by default; adjustable via contract to 7/14/30/90 days.
  * Backups/archival store: 30–90 days depending on SLAs; can be shortened with a contractual commitment.

- Evidence artifacts we can push now: short matrix PDF (attached), full subprocessor CSV (attached), and a one-page control mapping to MedicaCare SOC2/ISO control identifiers (if you provide the control list).

Connor — tagging you in case the procurement team asks for any network-level diagrams or SOC2 excerpts to include with the evidence bundle.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
